title: Latin circuits, Reidemeister, and the 3-nets that compose like cycles
claim: (1) If each range carries a proper pp-definable equivalence modulo which every circuit of every system is functional at each of its variables, the law composes like cycles; so a law composes like cycles with no overlapping circuit exactly when every circuit is a Latin hypercube modulo the tops (the Latin conjecture says overlapping never occurs). (2) For a Latin square, the relation of a 2x2 subsquare's entries is functional exactly when Reidemeister's condition holds, that is exactly for group isotopes. (3) The 3-net law of a finite abelian group composes like cycles exactly when the group is a p-group (its polymorphisms are the End(G)-affine maps, and a unique maximal proper fully invariant subgroup exists exactly for p-groups), and its systems then carry GF(p)-representable matroids. (4) If the elements with u^m = 1 generate a group without exhausting it (or two such sets do), its 3-net law does not compose like cycles: S3, D4, Z6. (5) No ternary polymorphism of the 3-net law of Q8 is a Mal'tsev operation modulo +-1 (an explicit 416-equation certificate); since census A found no failure for that law, either it fails in larger systems or Conjecture 7 of CYCLE-TOPS-20261021-001B-P001 is false.
failure_conditions: A law satisfying the hypothesis of (1) has a system whose circuits fail elimination.
A Latin square whose 2x2-subsquare relation is functional fails Reidemeister's condition or is not a group isotope, or the reverse.
A finite abelian p-group's 3-net law fails elimination, or a non-p-group's composes like cycles, or a polymorphism is not End(G)-affine.
A group as in (4) has a 3-net law that composes like cycles.
A ternary polymorphism of the Q8 3-net law is Mal'tsev modulo +-1, or the certificate's unknowns do not cancel.
foundation_claim_scope: Which laws compose like cycles: Latin circuits modulo the tops, and 3-net laws of Latin squares. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric distance or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py verifies Theorem 1's excluded value on all 8,202 circuit pairs of 1,200 fresh systems over the census survivors, Theorem 3 on 669 Latin squares (all of orders 3 and 4), Theorem 4's classification on 23 abelian groups of order 2 to 16, its polymorphism counts and the census tops, the gadget relations of Proposition 5 for S3, D4, Z6 and Q8, and Proposition 6's certificate with an independently built Q8; four controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive and randomized checks; the Reidemeister closure theorem and the circuits proof's Theorem 1 are cited; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: candidate-local-delta: Theorem 1, the abelian 3-net classification, the small-element obstruction and the Q8 separation are new to the program; Theorem 3 restates the classical Reidemeister closure theorem for circuits; Theorem 4 combines the circuits proof's Theorem 1 with a standard description of polymorphisms and of fully invariant subgroups, and an expert in Mal'tsev constraints would derive it quickly.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-21.
